title: Broken front tooth and a Danish dentist
summary: Edison tells how an English dentist broke his front tooth and how a Copenhagen dentist fixed it so he could work at Ronnie Scott's.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: So you really must have a good set of -- your teeth must be good.
I had teeth problems. I had some put in last summer. I went to a dentist in England. I had a cap right on my tooth, there in front, and he vanked on it so hard he

broke the tooth off. And it was right -- where I play, my embouchure is right there. I had to fly back to Copenhagen, and the dentist happened to be a saxophone player, so he knew the importance of my work to be done. And he put a temporary plate in there and I flew back to London, at Ronnie Scott's, and worked that night, you know.
It's quite a mental thing to know that your teeth are -- your teeth are all you have, you know, playing trumpet. Very important.
Sure. But the formation originally must have been right.

Oh, yes. Sure. Then I began to -- the mental stress it carries with it is absolutely -- you dream about losing your chops, you know. Because that's what happened to Bobby Moore. I took his place with Basie's band. He had sort of capped teeth, you know, and he went to a dentist and had them fixed and he never was able to play anymore.
But now, the dental industry has -- they have come a long way, you know.
Do you know about this guy in Boston?
No, I don't go to him.
Because that's where Trummy -- I think Trummy sent Pops up there, didn't he?
Pops, too, yeah. I think Pops went to that dentist, too.

But being out here in California and London, I couldn't go -- I had to have somebody right away. And this guy, this Danish guy, is fantastic. He's a good dentist, you know. And I happened to remember, Roy has had his whole thing -- the whole front part of his mouth, it's been a plate for years and years and years.
Yeah. So there are quite a few trumpet players that have caps, you know, on their teeth in front. So if they can do it, I said, well, I can do it myself. So it's --
Well, dentistry has advanced so much.
